knowledge-base.overview: Express.js 4.x/5.x guardrails, layered architecture (Controllers-Services-Repositories), middleware ordering, error handling, input validation, security hardening, and testing patterns. Applies to TypeScript-first REST APIs, web servers, and microservices built with Express.

core-principles.principle: Everything is middleware — parsing, auth, logging, validation, error handling. Compose small, focused middleware functions.
Controllers (thin, HTTP only) → Services (business logic) → Repositories (data access). No layer references what it should not know about.
Use TypeScript with strict mode for all new Express projects. No implicit any on req, res, or handler parameters.
helmet, cors, rate limiting, and input validation are required on every API — not optional.
Handle startup, shutdown, and uncaught errors properly. Never let the process crash silently.

guardrail.rule: Always call next(error) in async route handlers. Never swallow errors or let async exceptions go unhandled — they will crash the process or hang requests.

Use a centralized error-handling middleware with exactly 4 arguments (error, req, res, next). This is Express's signal that a function is an error handler. Register it last, after all routes and after notFoundHandler.
Validate and sanitize all user inputs with Zod (or Joi) at every API boundary before touching any service or database logic.
Use parameterized queries at all times. Never concatenate user input into SQL strings. Prefer Prisma, Knex parameterization, or prepared statements.
guardrail.bad: const user = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`);

guardrail.rule: Never expose stack traces or internal error details in production responses. Return generic messages to clients; log full context server-side.
Enable helmet() as the first middleware. It sets security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.) on every response.
Configure CORS with explicit allowed origins in production. Never use CORS origin '*' in production APIs.
guardrail.bad: app.use(cors()); // allows all origins in production

guardrail.rule: Implement rate limiting on all routes. Apply stricter limits on auth endpoints (login, register, password reset).
Services must contain business logic only. They must never reference req, res, or any Express types. This keeps services testable in isolation.
Controllers must be thin. They extract and validate inputs, call one service method, and return the response. No business logic in controllers.
Handle unhandledRejection and uncaughtException at process level. Log them with full context and exit cleanly on uncaughtException.
Implement graceful shutdown: close the HTTP server on SIGTERM/SIGINT and wait for in-flight requests to complete. Force-exit after a timeout.
Use compression middleware for response compression. Implement pagination for all list endpoints — never return unbounded result sets.
Set body parse size limits (express.json({ limit: '10mb' })) to prevent oversized payload attacks.
Use connection pooling for database connections. Never open a new connection per request.

project-structure.description: Standard Express + TypeScript layered API layout.
project-structure.example: my-api/ ├── src/ │ ├── app.ts # Express app (middleware, routes, error handling) │ ├── server.ts # Entry point (listen, graceful shutdown) │ ├── config/ │ │ └── index.ts # Environment and app configuration │ ├── controllers/ # Route handlers (thin, delegate to services) │ │ └── user.controller.ts │ ├── middlewares/ │ │ ├── auth.middleware.ts │ │ ├── error.middleware.ts │ │ ├── validate.middleware.ts │ │ └── rateLimit.middleware.ts │ ├── routes/ │ │ ├── index.ts # Aggregate all resource routes │ │ └── user.routes.ts │ ├── services/ # Business logic (no req/res) │ │ └── user.service.ts │ ├── repositories/ # Data access layer │ │ └── user.repository.ts │ ├── models/ # Data models / Prisma schema │ ├── schemas/ # Zod validation schemas │ │ └── user.schema.ts │ ├── types/ │ │ └── index.ts │ └── utils/ │ ├── errors.ts # AppError class │ └── logger.ts # Logger setup ├── tests/ │ └── user.test.ts ├── .env.example ├── package.json └── tsconfig.json

layer-responsibilities.layer: Knows: Controllers, middleware. Never: Services, repositories
Knows: Services, types. Never: Repositories, database
Knows: Repositories, types. Never: req/res, Express
Knows: Database client, types. Never: Services, controllers

pattern.name: App Configuration (src/app.ts)
pattern.description: Express app wiring: security, parsing, logging, routes, 404 handler, error handler. Order matters.

pattern.name: Server Entry Point (src/server.ts)
pattern.description: Binds the app to a port. Implements graceful shutdown and process-level error handlers.

middleware-order.description: Middleware must be registered in this order in app.ts. Sequence errors cause silent misfires (e.g. CORS headers missing, errors not caught).
middleware-order.step: errorHandler — centralized error handling (4-arg, must be last)

conventions.item: HTTP verbs map to CRUD: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (remove)
Apply auth middleware selectively — not on public routes
Apply validation middleware before the controller handler

testing.stack: Jest (test runner), Supertest (HTTP integration). Import app — not server — to avoid port conflicts.

rules.rule: One test file per resource or feature
Group by HTTP method and route using describe blocks
Test both success and error paths (validation failures, auth failures, not found)
Use beforeEach/afterEach for database cleanup in integration tests
Import app (not server) for supertest to avoid port conflicts

quick-reference.item: Thin: extract input, call service, return response. No business logic.
Business logic only. No req/res. No Express imports.
Data access only. Return domain types.
AppError class + centralized 4-arg errorHandler registered last
Always next(error) in async handlers — never swallow
Zod validate() middleware before every controller handler
Parameterized queries always — Prisma or prepared statements
helmet() + cors(explicit) + rate limiting on every app
Generic messages to clients; full context in server logs
Supertest + Jest; import app not server; test success + error paths
helmet → cors → json → morgan → routes → 404 → errorHandler
